decisions.decision: Does the plan need a review unit?

decisions.decision: Why is this plan in one linear chain with the other plans of the merge?
decisions.ruling: The 16 plans form one linear chain through requires. Most of them edit sync-engine/repo-sync or sync-engine/setup-sync, and parallel plans conflict there.

decisions.decision: Where do the tests of the new rules go?
decisions.ruling: This plan extends test:repo-sync with cases for its new rules. An existing case changes only where a ruling changes its expected result.

decisions.decision: Who runs mise run setup:configs in bootstrap and in the consumers?
decisions.ruling: The user, by hand, after the landing. It is out of scope, as in the earlier plans.
decisions.rejected: A unit or an after-landing step runs setup:configs.

decisions.decision: In which repo environments do [bootstrap.*] and [dotfiles] go?
decisions.ruling: Only in dev, like [tasks], when the tool is in dev. CI is not a machine to provision.

decisions.decision: How does the engine render <% %> in a [mise.*] string?
decisions.ruling: When the tools.toml of a tool contains <%, the engine renders that file as a gomplate template into a temp copy, and the generator reads the copy, so the generated file holds the rendered value. The render context has .config (the values of the tool), .all (the values of every selected tool) and .env (HOME, USER), on both sides. The overrides of the values file are not rendered. A <% %> expression sits inside a TOML basic string ("..."), and every string literal inside the expression is a Go raw string in backticks. A failed render (a required or test.Fail check) stops the mise config of that tool with code 2 on the current failure path: the existing conf.d files of the tool stay. A rendered copy that is not valid TOML gives the message <tools root>/<tool>/tools.toml: not valid TOML after render: <message>, code 2, for that tool.
decisions.rejected: Render the generated TOML output: data.ToTOML escapes the quotes inside an expression, so an expression such as required "message" .config.x breaks.

decisions.decision: What does the macos side of the generator write and refuse?
decisions.ruling: One file conf.d/<tool>/mise.toml for each tool with content. It writes every valid section, the dev-only sections included, because the Mac uses no environments. A [mise_env.*] table, the envs key of a mise tool and the requires_found key of a mise tool are tool errors: the files of that tool stay, the other tools continue, and the run returns 2. An [overrides.mise_env.*] table is a values-file error: the whole run stops with code 2 before any write. [overrides.mise.*] works as on the repo side, an override cannot add a key, and the comment is # override: macos.toml (the file name only).
decisions.rejected: Ignore envs and requires_found on the macos side.

decisions.ruling: [overrides.gitignore] and its checks, the setup-all and setup-<submodule> aliases of the mise tool (given to the library as a list of extra dev aliases), the records of the generated files for the file loop and the manifest, and the call of the library with side repo. Everything else of the mise generation, the env rules and the [overrides.mise*] checks moves to sync-engine/mise.
decisions.rejected: Move [overrides.gitignore] too; keep the env rules in repo-sync.

decisions.decision: Who builds the render context of a tools.toml that holds <%?
decisions.ruling: sync-engine/mise builds the context file itself for each tool whose tools.toml holds <%, from sync-engine/values, also when the tool has no .tmpl file. The file is in the work folder of the run; the library removes it after the render of that tool, and the exit trap removes the work folder.
decisions.rejected: Widen the P07 rule in repo-sync, which builds a context file only for a tool with a .tmpl file.

decisions.decision: Which [overrides] keys does the library read?
decisions.ruling: Only mise and mise_env. The Mac front-end (P09) stops with code 2 on [overrides.gitignore], as on any key that the Mac values file does not have.
decisions.rejected: The library also reads or refuses [overrides.gitignore].

decisions.decision: How does the engine generate the own [mise.*] config of a values file?
decisions.ruling: sync-engine/mise has a second entry for the own config of a values file. It generates the [mise.*] tables of the values file into <conf.d>/zz-macos/mise.toml, with the same section list, the header Synced from bootstrap: macos.toml [mise]. Do not edit this file. plus the second line The next sync replaces it, and a manual change is lost., and a render of <% %> with .all and .env (no .config). [overrides.mise.*] does not apply to it.
decisions.rejected: The Mac front-end builds the zz-macos file itself.

decisions.decision: Must a rendered value leave every fixed value of a tools.toml unchanged, and must the check use the parser of the generator (G7, G8)?
decisions.ruling: User ruling 2026-11-05: trust the values file. The check that the rendered copy has the same key paths as the raw tools.toml (78669ea) stands. A rendered value that replaces a fixed value with equal key paths, and a key that yq and gomplate read differently, are not defects, because a writer of the values file can already add mise config directly. A security review does not report these two cases again.
decisions.rejected: Require that each fixed value stays unchanged, and do the check with the parser of the generator: it adds engine code and tests and gives no real protection.
